title: the fire
hook: Sita answers, and walks into the fire

segments.voice: Yesterday: the fire began with words. Rama spoke coldly to Sita in front of everyone, and she wept. Did you think about how your words would land? A new week begins, with Sita's answer. Day six hundred fifty-nine.
screen: `NOT FOR YOU, BUT FOR MY HONOR.`

segments.voice: Sita wipes her tears. The crowd is silent. Monkeys, bears, rakshasas, Lakshmana, Sugriva, Vibhishana, all of them waiting. And when she speaks, in Valmiki, her voice is steady. She doesn't beg. She doesn't apologize. She asks her husband a question: why are you talking to me the way a common man talks to a common woman? Then, point by point, in front of the same crowd that heard him, she answers everything he said.
screen: `SHE WIPES HER TEARS.` → `SHE DOESN'T BEG.` → `POINT BY POINT.`

segments.voice: What was in my power, she says, my heart, was always yours. When I was seized, my body was not in my power. Whose fault is that? And if you meant to give me up, why didn't you tell Hanuman when he found me? I would have let go of my life then, and spared you a war. Then she turns to Lakshmana and asks him to build a fire. Lakshmana looks at his brother, angry and pained, and Rama gives a sign. Lakshmana builds it. Sita walks around Rama in a circle of respect. She folds her hands and calls on Agni, the god of fire, the witness of every vow: if my heart has never turned from Rama, protect me. And she walks into the flames. The crowd cries out. In that moment, Valmiki says, the gods come down: Brahma, Shiva, Indra and others, and Brahma tells Rama who he really is, Vishnu himself. Then Agni rises out of the fire, holding Sita, unharmed, her clothes and garlands untouched, and declares her pure. Rama answers that he never doubted her, but the world had to see it. Hindus have read this scene in many ways. In some later tellings, like the Adhyatma Ramayana and Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, the real Sita had been kept safe inside the fire all along, and only a shadow was taken to Lanka; the fire simply gives her back. Others hold to Valmiki's version, and honor Sita's courage in it. And many readers today linger longest on her answer. Valmiki gave her those words. They're still there.
screen: `MY HEART WAS ALWAYS YOURS.` · `LAKSHMANA BUILDS THE FIRE.` · `AGNI GIVES HER BACK.` · `A SHADOW SITA, IN LATER TELLINGS.` · then, large: `VALMIKI GAVE HER THOSE WORDS.`

segments.voice: Sit up gently, with a straight, easy back. Think of something that is truly yours, that nobody can take: a value, a love, a promise you've kept. Name it to yourself. Breathe in, and feel how steady it is. Breathe out, and let anything others have said about you fall away, just for now. Rest in what you know is true. The bell holds the time.
The fire. Sita answers Rama point by point, walks into the flames calling Agni to witness, and Agni himself gives her back, unharmed.
Your line: Agni gives her back. Today, when someone misjudges you, answer calmly with what you know is true. Day six hundred fifty-nine.

howItsDone: The agni-parīkṣā, Sita's trial by fire, is retold and debated in Hindu homes, temples, classrooms and women's songs; different Ramayanas tell it differently, and many tellers dwell on Sita's own words.

pairs: builds the fire at a sign from Rama

myth: Sita begs Rama to take her back
she answers him point by point and asks for a fire.
Agni returns Sita unharmed and declares her pure
she rises from the flames with her clothes and garlands untouched.
every Ramayana tells the fire the same way
some later tellings say a shadow Sita was taken, and the real one kept in the fire.

fork.setup: you're Sita. your husband has questioned you in public. what do you do?
options: answer him point by point, then call on the fire to witness.
fork.reveal: she answers every charge, has Lakshmana build a fire, calls on Agni, and walks in; Agni gives her back.

original.note: Sanskrit agniparīkṣā: the trial by fire, from agni, fire, and parīkṣā, test or examination.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sita silently accepted a test.
what it means: she challenged Rama's words first, then called the fire to witness her truth.
what a scholar hears: the Adhyatma Ramayana and the Ramcharitmanas tell of a shadow Sita taken to Lanka; Valmiki has no shadow.

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Sita's speech (heart in her power, body not; why not tell Hanuman): paraphrased; confirm.
The gods who appear (Brahma, Shiva, Indra and others): confirm. Dasharatha's appearance (Yuddha 119) is kept for day 660.
Rama's reply that he never doubted her but the world had to see: paraphrased; confirm.
Shadow Sita (Māyā-Sītā / chāyā-Sītā) attributed to the Adhyatma Ramayana and the Ramcharitmanas; confirm the kandas.
